note: Year 10 Higher Higher Spring Block 6 Interpret and represent data: one set of templates per small step of the scheme of learning.

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S1 Averages and range
templates.text: Here are five numbers: [[x3]], [[x1]], [[x5]], [[x2]], [[x4]]. Work out (a) the mean (b) the median (c) the mode (d) the range.

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S1 Averages and range
templates.text: Here are six numbers: [[x4]], [[x1]], [[x6]], [[x2]], [[x5]], [[x3]]. Work out the median and the range.
templates.answer: Median [[(x3 + x4) / 2]], range [[x6 - x1]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S1 Averages and range
templates.text: The mean of five numbers is [[m]]. Four of the numbers are [[a]], [[b]], [[c]] and [[d]]. Work out the fifth number.

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S1 Averages and range
templates.text: The mean of four numbers is [[m]]. A fifth number is added and the mean of the five numbers becomes [[m2]]. Work out the fifth number. (3 marks)

templates.subtopic: Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S2 Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.text: The table shows the number of goals scored in some matches. (a) What is the mode? (b) How many matches were played?

templates.subtopic: Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S2 Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.text: The table shows the number of goals scored in some matches. Work out the mean number of goals. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

templates.subtopic: Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S2 Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.text: The table shows the number of goals scored in some matches. Work out the median number of goals.

templates.subtopic: Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S2 Averages from an ungrouped frequency table
templates.text: The table shows the number of goals scored in matches. The mean is 1.5. Work out the missing frequency $x$. (3 marks)

templates.subtopic: Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S3 Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.text: The table shows how long some people waited. (a) Write down the modal class. (b) Work out an estimate of the mean time. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

templates.subtopic: Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S3 Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.text: The table shows how long some people waited. Complete the working: the midpoint of the class 10 ≤ t < 20 is 15. Work out an estimate of the total waiting time and the mean.
templates.answer: Total ≈ [[5 * f1 + 15 * f2 + 25 * f3 + 35 * f4]] minutes from [[f1 + f2 + f3 + f4]] people, mean ≈ [[(5 * f1 + 15 * f2 + 25 * f3 + 35 * f4) / (f1 + f2 + f3 + f4)|dp:1]] minutes

templates.subtopic: Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S3 Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.text: Explain why the mean worked out from a grouped frequency table is only an estimate.
templates.answer: We do not know the actual values in each class, so we use the midpoint of the class as an estimate (here [[f1 + f2 + f3 + f4]] people, mean ≈ [[(5 * f1 + 15 * f2 + 25 * f3 + 35 * f4) / (f1 + f2 + f3 + f4)|dp:1]])

templates.subtopic: Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S3 Mean from a grouped frequency table
templates.text: The table shows how long some people waited. (a) Estimate the mean waiting time. (b) The target is a mean of less than [[tg]] minutes. Is it met? Explain. (4 marks)
templates.answer: (a) [[(5 * f1 + 15 * f2 + 25 * f3 + 35 * f4) / (f1 + f2 + f3 + f4)|dp:1]] minutes  (b) [[(5 * f1 + 15 * f2 + 25 * f3 + 35 * f4) / (f1 + f2 + f3 + f4) < tg|if:Yes: the estimated mean is below the target/No: the estimated mean is not below the target]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S4 Use data to compare distributions
templates.text: Class A: mean [[m1]], range [[r1]]. Class B: mean [[m2]], range [[r2]]. Compare the two classes.
templates.answer: Class [[m1 > m2|if:A/B]] has the higher mean (better on average); class [[r1 < r2|if:A/B]] has the smaller range (more consistent)

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S4 Use data to compare distributions
templates.text: The mean time for Ali is [[m1]] seconds and the range is [[r1]]. For Ben the mean is [[m2]] seconds and the range is [[r2]]. Who is faster on average? Who is more consistent?
templates.answer: [[m1 < m2|if:Ali/Ben]] is faster on average; [[r1 < r2|if:Ali/Ben]] is more consistent

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S4 Use data to compare distributions
templates.text: Team A scored [[a1]], [[a2]], [[a3]], [[a4]], [[a5]] points. Team B scored [[b1]], [[b2]], [[b3]], [[b4]], [[b5]]. Compare the teams using the mean and the range.
templates.answer: A: mean [[(a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5) / 5|dp:1]], range [[max(max(a1, a2), max(a3, max(a4, a5))) - min(min(a1, a2), min(a3, min(a4, a5)))]]; B: mean [[(b1 + b2 + b3 + b4 + b5) / 5|dp:1]], range [[max(max(b1, b2), max(b3, max(b4, b5))) - min(min(b1, b2), min(b3, min(b4, b5)))]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S4 Use data to compare distributions
templates.text: Two bus companies record how many minutes late their buses are. Company X: mean [[m1]], range [[r1]]. Company Y: mean [[m2]], range [[r2]]. Which company would you use to be on time? Give two reasons. (3 marks)
templates.answer: [[m1 + r1 < m2 + r2|if:Company X/Company Y]]: [[m1 < m2|if:X/Y]] has the lower mean lateness and [[r1 < r2|if:X/Y]] has the smaller range (more consistent)

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S5 Sampling
templates.text: A school has [[N]] pupils. A random sample of [[n]] pupils is taken. What fraction of the pupils is in the sample?
templates.answer: $[[n / N|frac]]$

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S5 Sampling
templates.text: A school has [[b]] boys and [[g]] girls. A stratified sample of [[n]] pupils is taken. How many boys and girls are in the sample?
templates.answer: Boys [[n * b / (b + g)|dp:0]], girls [[n * g / (b + g)|dp:0]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S5 Sampling
templates.text: A survey about [[tp]] only asks pupils in the lunch queue. Explain why the sample may be biased and say how to improve it.
templates.answer: Pupils who are not in the queue are left out, so it is not representative; take a random sample from the school register

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S5 Sampling
templates.text: A town has [[a]] adults and [[c]] children. A stratified sample of [[n]] people is taken. Work out how many adults and children, and explain why this is fair. (3 marks)
templates.answer: Adults [[n * a / (a + c)|dp:0]], children [[n * c / (a + c)|dp:0]]: each group is represented in proportion to its size

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S6 Types of data
templates.text: Is [[k == 0|if:the number of pupils in a class/]][[k == 1|if:the time taken to run 100 m/]][[k == 2|if:a pupil's favourite sport/]][[k == 3|if:the height of a tree/]][[k == 4|if:shoe size/]][[k == 5|if:eye colour/]][[k == 6|if:the mass of a parcel/]][[k == 7|if:the number of goals in a match/]] categorical, discrete or continuous?
templates.answer: [[k == 0 || k == 4 || k == 7|if:discrete/]][[k == 1 || k == 3 || k == 6|if:continuous/]][[k == 2 || k == 5|if:categorical/]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S6 Types of data
templates.text: Is [[k == 0|if:the number of pupils in a class/]][[k == 1|if:the time taken to run 100 m/]][[k == 2|if:a pupil's favourite sport/]][[k == 3|if:the height of a tree/]][[k == 4|if:shoe size/]][[k == 5|if:eye colour/]][[k == 6|if:the mass of a parcel/]][[k == 7|if:the number of goals in a match/]] qualitative or quantitative data?
templates.answer: [[k == 2 || k == 5|if:Qualitative/Quantitative]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S6 Types of data
templates.text: Mia says that [[k == 0|if:the number of pupils in a class/]][[k == 1|if:the time taken to run 100 m/]][[k == 2|if:a pupil's favourite sport/]][[k == 3|if:the height of a tree/]][[k == 4|if:shoe size/]][[k == 5|if:eye colour/]][[k == 6|if:the mass of a parcel/]][[k == 7|if:the number of goals in a match/]] is continuous data because it is a number. Is she right? Explain.
templates.answer: [[k == 0 || k == 4 || k == 7|if:No: it is discrete, it can only take particular values/Not always: only some numerical data is continuous]] (this one is [[k == 0 || k == 4 || k == 7|if:discrete/]][[k == 1 || k == 3 || k == 6|if:continuous/]][[k == 2 || k == 5|if:categorical/]])

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S6 Types of data
templates.text: Give one example each of discrete, continuous and categorical data from a survey about [[k == 0|if:school/]][[k == 1|if:sport/]][[k == 2|if:shopping/]]. (3 marks)
templates.answer: e.g. discrete: a count such as the number of items; continuous: a measurement such as a time or length; categorical: a colour, type or name

templates.text: The bar chart shows the number of books read by pupils in a month. How many pupils read 6 to 10 books?

templates.subtopic: Averages from a grouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S7 Averages from a grouped frequency table
templates.text: The bar chart shows the number of books read by pupils in a month. Which is the modal class?

templates.subtopic: Averages from a grouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S7 Averages from a grouped frequency table
templates.text: The bar chart shows the number of books read by pupils in a month. How many pupils read more than 10 books? How many pupils were surveyed?
templates.answer: [[f3 + f4]] pupils read more than 10; [[f1 + f2 + f3 + f4]] pupils in total

templates.subtopic: Averages from a grouped frequency table
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S7 Averages from a grouped frequency table
templates.text: The bar chart shows the number of books read by pupils in a month. (a) What fraction of the pupils read 11 or more books? Give your answer in its simplest form. (b) What percentage read 5 books or fewer, to 1 decimal place? (3 marks)

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S8 Capture and recapture
templates.text: [[m]] fish are caught, marked and released. Later [[n]] fish are caught and [[k]] are marked. Estimate the number of fish in the lake.

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S8 Capture and recapture
templates.text: A biologist marks [[m]] birds. A second sample of [[n]] birds contains [[k]] marked birds. Estimate the population.

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S8 Capture and recapture
templates.text: In a capture-recapture survey [[m]] animals are marked, then a sample of [[n]] has [[k]] marked. Estimate the population and give two assumptions you made.
templates.answer: [[m * n / k]]; the marked animals mixed evenly and the population did not change (no births, deaths or migration)

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S8 Capture and recapture
templates.text: A lake has an estimated population of [[N]] fish using capture-recapture. A second survey marks [[m]] fish, and [[n]] fish in the next sample include [[k]] marked. Work out the new estimate and the difference from [[N]]. (3 marks)
templates.answer: New estimate [[m * n / k]]; difference [[abs(m * n / k - N)]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S9 Scatter graphs
templates.text: The scatter graph shows revision time and test score for 8 pupils. What score did the pupil who revised for [[k]] hours get?

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S9 Scatter graphs
templates.text: The scatter graph shows revision time and test score for 8 pupils. How many pupils revised for more than [[k]] hours?

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S9 Scatter graphs
templates.text: The scatter graph shows revision time and test score (out of [[ymax]]) for 8 pupils. Describe how the test score changes as revision time increases.
templates.answer: As the hours of revision go up, the test score goes up

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S9 Scatter graphs
templates.text: The scatter graph shows revision time and test score for 8 pupils. (a) Estimate the score of a pupil who revised for 5 hours. (b) Pupil X revised for 9 hours. Explain why you should not use the graph to predict X's score. (3 marks)
templates.answer: (a) about [[m * 5 + c]]  (b) 9 hours is outside the range of the data (1 to 8 hours)

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S10 Interpolation and extrapolation
templates.text: A line of best fit has equation $y = [[m]]x + [[c]]$. Use it to predict $y$ when $x = [[x0]]$.

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S10 Interpolation and extrapolation
templates.text: The data covers $x$ from [[lo]] to [[hi]]. Is a prediction at $x = [[x0]]$ interpolation or extrapolation?
templates.answer: [[x0 >= lo && x0 <= hi|if:Interpolation: inside the data range/Extrapolation: outside the data range]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S10 Interpolation and extrapolation
templates.text: A line of best fit $y = [[m]]x + [[c]]$ is based on $x$ from [[lo]] to [[hi]]. Predict $y$ at $x = [[x0]]$ and say whether you can trust it.
templates.answer: [[m * x0 + c]]; [[x0 >= lo && x0 <= hi|if:fairly reliable as it is inside the data/less reliable as it is outside the data]]

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B6 Interpret and represent data · S10 Interpolation and extrapolation
templates.text: Ice cream sales (y) against temperature (x) follow $y = [[m]]x - [[c]]$ for temperatures from [[lo]]°C to [[hi]]°C. (a) Predict sales at [[x0]]°C. (b) Explain why predicting sales at [[x1]]°C may be unreliable. (3 marks)
templates.answer: (a) [[m * x0 - c]]  (b) [[x1]]°C is outside the range of the data, so the pattern may not continue
